goal: Research Codex automations vs Claude routines for Azoth governed synthesis bus and continuation layer
refresh_summary: First durable capture of the April 2026 automation-control-plane research. This capsule preserves the current thesis, the three-lane model, and the next research threads so future passes can refine or digest them instead of rebuilding context from chat history.
limitations: OpenAI and Anthropic automation surfaces are temporally unstable; claims were checked against official pages observed on 2026-04-21 local time.
Repo-local findings describe the current Azoth snapshot only and may age as control-plane and automation slices land.
This capsule is discovery-only. It does not authorize implementation, governance mutation, or unattended side effects.

questions.question: Can this Codex-vs-Claude automation research capsule be reused for follow-on architecture and proposal work?
What is the strongest current framing for Azoth after comparing Codex automations with Claude routines and continuation surfaces?

thesis: Azoth should not become a raw message bus. The strongest current framing is a governed synthesis bus plus continuation layer: orchestrator-subagent for active reasoning, shared state for durable truth, narrow producer automations for evidence, thread-bound wakeups for continuation, and only a bounded advance-by-contract lane for automatic progression.

decisions_locked.primary_framing: governed synthesis bus plus continuation layer

lane_model.evidence_producers: Narrow automations or routines gather facts, statuses, alerts, review outcomes, and other evidence. They are not authorities by default.
lane_model.wakeup_and_continuation: Thread-bound wakeups or equivalent continuation surfaces re-enter an existing run, check objective predicates, and either continue, report, or stop.
lane_model.automatic_advance: Automatic advancement is only safe as advance-by-contract: same approved goal, same or narrower scope, predeclared next stage, objective stop conditions, and fail-closed behavior on ambiguity.

automatic_advance_constraints: No scope extension without a new explicit human approval.
No direct memory or governance mutation from producer automations.
No silent continuation after request-changes, critical review findings, expired gates, or stale continuation predicates.
No autonomous side effects based on narrative inference alone; the next executable stage must already be represented in durable state.

platform_comparison.codex_default_role: Best default control plane for Azoth's current posture because thread automations preserve conversation continuity, background automations report into Triage, and the surface already fits review-and-reentry more naturally than cloud-fresh autonomous sessions.
platform_comparison.claude_default_role: Not the default continuation layer. Claude scheduled tasks and routines are still valuable comparison surfaces, with routines especially interesting as a future ingress worker lane.
platform_comparison.claude_future_experimental_ingress_lane: Claude routines look strongest when the problem is external event ingress or cloud-triggered work initiation, not when the main requirement is durable in-thread continuation under the current Azoth trust model.

preliminary_merge_research.current_position: Pre-authorized merge is worth researching, but it should not enter the first automatic-advance lane unless the merge policy becomes explicit, mechanically checkable, and fail-closed.
candidate_predicates: The PR is mergeable according to the host.
No blocking review threads or unresolved required changes remain.
The governing approval has not expired and still covers the intended merge action.
No new critical findings or scope drift appeared after the last approved checkpoint.
main_risks: Confusing outdated or non-blocking review comments with real blockers.
Advancing from stale CI or stale review state.
Letting automation infer policy exceptions that should remain human-owned.

sources.title: Codex automations documentation
sources.published_context: Official OpenAI developer documentation observed on 2026-04-21
findings: Codex distinguishes thread automations from standalone or project automations.
Thread automations are the closest match to wakeup-style continuation because they reuse an existing conversation thread.
Standalone and project automations align more naturally with recurring producer lanes and review surfaces such as Triage.

sources.title: Codex for (almost) everything
findings: OpenAI explicitly described Codex automations as able to reuse existing conversation threads and wake automatically for long-term work.
That product framing reinforces Codex as a continuation primitive rather than only a scheduler.

sources.title: Introducing the Codex app
findings: The launch framing positioned automations as background work whose results flow back into a review queue.
This strengthens the evidence-producer and review-reentry interpretation.

sources.title: Multi-agent coordination patterns
findings: Anthropic recommends starting with orchestrator-subagent for the broadest range of problems.
The article presents message bus as useful for event-driven pipelines and shared state as useful for collaborative accumulation.
It also warns that message-bus routing can fail silently and that shared-state systems need explicit termination conditions.

sources.title: Claude Code scheduled tasks
findings: Scheduled tasks and loop-style polling are the closest Claude continuation analogue to Codex thread wakeups.
These surfaces are useful for bounded re-entry but are still distinct from routines.

sources.title: Claude Code routines
findings: Routines are triggered by schedule, API, or GitHub events and run on Anthropic-managed infrastructure.
Routines are better understood as cloud-triggered ingress workers than as thread-preserving continuation.
The documentation states there are no approval prompts during a run, which increases autonomy but sits in tension with Azoth's current trust posture.

repo_findings: Azoth today is already closest to orchestrator-subagent plus shared-state continuity, not a raw message-bus runtime.
The repo already carries an emergent narrow-producer plus separate-synthesizer pattern for automation-driven insight generation.
Durable waiting and re-entry already appear as a real need in the PR publish reflections, especially around CI polling and review completion.
The current Codex adapter is intentionally fail-closed about staged delegation and should remain so if automation-backed continuation expands.
Run-ledger and resume semantics already provide the strongest local foundation for bounded automatic advancement.

findings: Azoth is protocol-first with Codex and Claude Code as co-primary platforms.
The shared state layer is explicit and harness-specific mechanics are only the enforcement layer.
Codex parity mode already requires staged pipeline execution and a stop when staged delegation is unavailable.
That existing contract argues against silent automation-driven inline collapse.
Human gates stop the pipeline, and governed continuation must consume approval through the run ledger rather than narrative continuation.
Replay is bounded and fail-closed rather than open-ended.
The run ledger already models paused human gates, pending stages, and explicit approval consumption.
This is the strongest local anchor for a future advance-by-contract lane.
The repo already records the design judgment that narrow domain automations should feed a separate synthesis authority before anything reaches the governed inbox.
The repo already records durable waiting and re-entry as necessary for PR publish flows and identifies merge policy as a separate explicit concern.

open_research_threads: Define the exact contract for a wakeup-triggered continuation record: dedupe key, evidence payload, stop conditions, and freshness windows.
Research a pre-authorized merge policy that is narrow enough to be mechanical and fail-closed rather than narrative or discretionary.
Clarify whether Codex thread automations can act as the default continuation lane while Claude routines remain a future ingress lane.
Decide how synthesis authority should summarize repeated low-level signals without turning the inbox into a noisy event sink.
